speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To help me narrow down the cause, can you tell me how long this has been going on and if you have noticed any redness or warmth in the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Gamekeeper's Thumb (Stener lesion) or Skier's Thumb (Ulnar collateral ligament injury) of the thumb, though the patient reports ring finger involvement, suggesting a potential misidentification of the injured digit or a distinct injury such as a mallet finger or tendon rupture of the ring finger. Given the mechanism (forceful pull) and location, further clarification is needed to confirm the exact digit and nature of the injury.

REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray of right hand (AP and lateral views).

REQUEST TEST: Clinical examination of the right ring finger and thumb for stability and tenderness.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
